title: Graceful stream teardown, retry/backpressure policy, and partial-generation cleanup
creator: Priya Shah
description: Problem: When clients disconnect (TCP/HTTP/WS) or encounter client-side timeouts while a model is streaming a generation, the runtime must: 1) stop wasting GPU cycles on work that will never be consumed, 2) leave the system in a consistent state for tool/function calling and structured outputs, 3) surface traceable partial outputs for debugging and billing reconciliation, and 4) avoid double-executing external tools or side effects if the client reconnects or retries. Current behavior: connections are often torn down immediately and model tokens continue until kernel cancellation hits, KV cache may remain pinned, tool calls may have been issued without a clear retry/idempotency strategy, and downstream consumers can get broken JSON fragments. This ticket defines a design and implementation plan for a graceful teardown and retry/backpressure policy for streaming endpoints.
acceptance_criteria: Server cancels active generation within the configured grace window (default 5s) after client disconnect and reports cancellation reason in logs and traces
Partial generation artifacts are persisted to ephemeral store for at least 60s and accessible via admin API for debugging
Tool/function calls triggered during a streaming request are guarded by an idempotency key derived from request id + sequence number; replays must not double-execute side effects
Structured output mode wraps partial chunks with metadata so downstream parsers can detect incomplete JSON and either wait for continuation or fetch stored partials
Billing is aligned: tokens generated after grace window are not charged to the client; audit trail records token windows and decision to cancel
E2E tests exist that simulate abrupt client disconnect, slow client (backpressure), and reconnect-with-resume scenarios; all tests pass in CI and on staging at 10k RPS load profile
Dashboard exposes metrics: stream_disconnect_rate, avg_time_to_cancel, orphaned_kv_cache_entries, partial_persist_rate
implementation_notes: Introduce per-stream lifecycle states: OPEN -> DRAINING (grace window) -> CANCELLED -> CLEANED
On transport disconnect event: transition to DRAINING, send SIG_CANCEL to model runtime after grace window if client hasn't reconnected
Make kernels responsive to cancellation token and ensure KV cache eviction occurs on CLEANED state to free pinned memory
Add a small ephemeral persistence layer (s3-like or in-cluster blob store) for partial chunks with TTL; include content-addressable keys and request-id indexing
Extend existing stream chunk schema to include metadata: {seq, partial: true|false, continuation_token, checksum}
For function/tool-calling flows, generate an idempotency key at the point of scheduling the external call; store call metadata in call-log store and mark call state atomically

Compatibility layer: older single-response clients should receive a final aggregated payload when a stream ends; structured-output clients should receive chunked metadata to assemble or fetch missing pieces
Design trade-off: longer grace window reduces accidental cancellation for flaky networks but increases wasted GPU time — default 5s with per-customer override recommended
Operational: add alerting on orphaned sessions > 2 minutes and high rate of partial_persist events to detect regressions
Backwards compatibility: keep current non-streaming endpoints unchanged; streaming semantics only affect streaming routes and clients opting in
tasks: Spike (1): implement transport disconnect hooks and graceful state machine in serving runtime
Spike (2): prototype ephemeral partial-persist store and admin fetch API
Implement: kernel cancellation path and KV cache eviction on CLEANED
Implement: idempotency keys for external tool calls and call-log storage
SDKs: add client-side reconnect and resume logic (JS + Python) using continuation_token
Tests: unit tests for state transitions, integration tests with mock tool endpoints, load test on staging
Docs: design doc + updated API spec for chunk metadata and compatibility notes
Rollout: feature flag gating, staged rollout to 10% tenants, then ramp based on metrics
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Partial persistence increases storage/Audit surface; Mitigation: TTL 60s by default and compact background job
Risk: Idempotency key misuse could block legitimate retries; Mitigation: include nonce+timestamp and make key expiration configurable
Risk: Longer grace windows increase GPU cost; Mitigation: per-customer policy and default conservative 5s
Risk: Structured-output parsers may break on metadata; Mitigation: provide SDK helpers and backward-compatible aggregator endpoint
progress_updates: 2026-03-01: Ticket created after postmortem from PROD incident where several streams continued generating after client timeout (on-call: Alex Kim)
2026-03-03: Spike #1 complete. Implemented prototype state machine in local serving runtime; observed kernel cancellation latency ~120ms on n1-standard testbed
2026-03-06: Design review with runtime, SDK, and PM teams. Agreed on 5s default grace window and ephemeral store TTL 60s. Action: PR for chunk metadata schema
2026-03-09: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/PR-1418 (draft) implementing transport hooks and chunk metadata. Seeking runtime and security review
2026-03-12: Integrated idempotency plumbing for tool-calls; created call-log prototype backed by existing metadata DB. Work remaining: atomic persistence and SDK resume APIs
2026-03-14: Running load tests on staging with simulated disconnects; initial metrics show avg_time_to_cancel 4.8s, partial_persist_rate 0.6% at 10k RPS
notes_for_release: Feature gated behind runtime.feature.graceful_stream_teardown. Default off for existing customers; enable for new streaming tenants and run a 2-week canary. Update SDK versions to include resume helpers before enabling for public traffic. Monitor stream_disconnect_rate and avg_time_to_cancel closely during ramp.
